headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,535 AS US-IRAN PRELIMINARY DEAL EASES SAFE-HAVEN BID; MONTHLY DECLINE LOOMS
snippet: Gold spot slipped to $4,535 on May 31 as reports of a preliminary US-Iran peace agreement eased safe-haven demand; the metal remains on track for a 0.8% monthly decline, pressured by three-year-high US inflation data and Fed rate hold expectations well into 2027.

headline: GOLDSEEK COT MAY 29: SPECS TRIM GOLD LONGS AHEAD OF JUNE — SILVER POSITIONING STAYS CAUTIOUS
snippet: The May 29 Commitment of Traders report shows speculative money trimming net gold positions heading into June while silver net longs and the USDX positioning signal a cautious bias; commercial hedgers remain heavily short gold, a historical precursor to institutional profit-taking that retail investors should watch.

headline: SILVER: SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT AT 46M OZ — SOLAR AND AI MAKE THE SUPPLY GAP STRUCTURALLY PERMANENT
snippet: The Silver Institute's 2026 World Silver Survey confirmed a sixth consecutive global supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces, with cumulative above-ground stock draws since 2021 reaching 762 million oz; because 70% of silver is mined as a by-product, supply cannot respond to higher prices — making the deficit structural rather than cyclical, with year-end targets near $110.

headline: COPPER CHARGES TO $6.42 — SECOND STRAIGHT MONTHLY ADVANCE AS AI GRID BUILD-OUT SWAMPS CHILE OUTPUT CUTS
snippet: Copper futures held at $6.42/lb at May month-end, on track for a second consecutive monthly gain, as AI data-centre construction and global power-grid electrification demand outpaced production constraints from Chilean refiners; J.P. Morgan estimates data-centre copper demand alone reaches 475,000 metric tons in 2026, with a projected 3-million-tonne cumulative concentrate deficit by 2036.

headline: LITHIUM TIPS INTO FIRST DEFICIT: ENERGY STORAGE DEMAND JUMPS 55% YOY — BATTERY CARBONATE NEAR $25,000/T
snippet: 2026 marks lithium's structural inflection: stationary energy storage demand is up 55% year-over-year, global consumption grows 13.5% while supply grows only 9.9%, pointing to a 22,000–80,000 metric ton deficit; battery-grade lithium carbonate spot reached $25,156/t in April as upstream spodumene tightened on converter overcapacity.

headline: BAYHORSE SILVER (TSXV: BHS) FIRES UP 2,000m UNDERGROUND DRILL JUNE 1 — TARGETING 6.3M OZ RESOURCE EXTENSIONS
snippet: Bayhorse Silver Inc. (TSXV: BHS) announced May 28 that underground preparations are complete at its Oregon silver mine, with a 2,000-metre Phase 1 diamond drill program starting June 1; the first 13 holes will test CR-2 and IP anomalies to seek extensions of the NI 43-101 inferred 6.3 million-ounce silver resource.

headline: NO DEAL ON RARE EARTHS: CHINA HOLDS FIRM POST TRUMP-XI SUMMIT; AUSTRALIA BOOTS CHINESE INVESTORS FROM NORTHERN MINERALS
snippet: China's rare earth export controls covering 12+ elements showed no sign of easing following the May 14-15 Trump-Xi summit; Australia responded by ordering six Chinese-linked shareholders in Northern Minerals to divest their stakes within two weeks, as US indium imports from China have collapsed 77% since February 2025 controls were introduced.

headline: URANIUM ABOVE $85 — META'S 1.2GW NUCLEAR CAMPUS AND DENISON'S PHOENIX GROUNDBREAKING SIGNAL STRUCTURAL DEMAND SHIFT
snippet: Spot uranium held above $85/lb — up 18.9% year-over-year — as Meta's partnership with Oklo for a 1.2 GW nuclear campus in Ohio and Kazatomprom's new India supply agreements confirmed AI data centres as the structural demand driver through the 2030s; Denison Mines' Phoenix project became the first Canadian uranium mine to break ground in over a decade.

headline: EQUINOX SWALLOWS ORLA IN $5.1B ALL-SHARE DEAL: WHAT IT MEANS FOR JUNIOR MINERS AND WHO'S NEXT
snippet: Equinox Gold's $5.1 billion all-share acquisition of Orla Mining — backed by Pierre Lassonde and Fairfax Financial, with a July shareholder vote pending — creates a US$18.5 billion North American gold producer at 1.1 million oz/year; the deal sets a valuation template for underfollowed TSXV juniors that could be next in the consolidation wave.

headline: GOLD MINERS UP 50% YTD WHILE S&P 500 SINKS 10%: THE EQUITY-TO-METAL DISCONNECT IS FINALLY CLOSING
snippet: The Gold Miners Index (GDM) registered approximately 50% year-to-date gains through April 2026 while the S&P 500 declined roughly 10%; analysts attribute the divergence to operational leverage at record gold prices, industry-wide all-in costs below $2,000/oz, and a long-overdue sector re-rating as price-deck assumptions are revised above $4,500 for 2026-2029.

headline: ASX 200 MINING SHARES SMASH MULTI-YEAR HIGHS IN MAY 2026 AS IRON ORE, COPPER, AND GOLD SURGE SIMULTANEOUSLY
snippet: ASX 200 mining shares hit multi-year highs in May 2026 as iron ore, lithium, copper, and gold surged on simultaneous demand signals; Australian-listed miners are benefiting disproportionately from China's infrastructure stimulus and accelerating rare earth supply diversification pressure on the sector.

headline: EXPLORATION BUDGETS UP 11% BUT DISCOVERY RATES KEEP FALLING — ADJACENT JUNIOR PLAYS ARE 2026'S SMART MONEY TARGET
snippet: Global mining exploration budgets climbed 11% to US$6.2 billion with gold taking the largest share, yet the discovery rate per exploration dollar has declined for the fifth consecutive year; junior explorers with projects adjacent to major established mines — offering built-in geology, infrastructure, and acquisition logic — are emerging as the high-conviction play for retail investors in 2026.
